Change c0429. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. V; 1831 Ch. XXII.

Context before (unchanged): "Explanation! you may possibly say; what can Elizabeth have to explain?

1818 text: If you really say this, my questions are answered, and I have no more to do than to sign myself your affectionate cousin.

1831 text: If you really say this, my questions are answered, and all my doubts satisfied.

Diff: If you really say this, my questions are answered, and [-I have no more to do than to sign myself your affectionate cousin-] {+all my doubts satisfied+} .

Context after (unchanged): But you are distant from me, and it is possible that you may dread, and yet be pleased with this explanation; and, in a probability of this being the case, I dare not any longer postpone writing what, during your absence, I have often wished to express to you, but have never had the courage to begin.

result.rationale: Replaces the 1818 sign-off "I have no more to do than to sign myself your affectionate cousin" with "all my doubts satisfied." This drops Elizabeth's self-presentation as Victor's cousin and foregrounds her inner doubts, changing how she stands toward him.
